notes:
The repository is not a device. It is the C++ Gazebo Sensors library of sensor models, not a runnable sensor, device server, ROS node or steppable environment. README.md:18-20 states: 'Gazebo Sensors, a component of Gazebo, provides numerous sensor models designed to generate realistic data from simulation environments. Gazebo Sensors is used in conjunction with Gazebo Libraries, and especially relies on the rendering capabilities from Gazebo Rendering and physics simulation from Gazebo Physics.' The root CMakeLists.txt:1-6 names project gz-sensors VERSION 11.0.0; src/CMakeLists.txt:55-228 builds only gz_add_component libraries (rendering, camera, depth_camera, dvl, lidar, gpu_lidar, logical_camera, magnetometer, imu, cpu_lidar, altimeter, air_pressure, air_speed, force_torque, navsat, rgbd_camera, thermal_camera, boundingbox_camera, segmentation_camera, wide_angle_camera), and src/CMakeLists.txt:230-236 adds only gtest targets. No executable device entry point exists. The only non-test executables are examples: examples/save_image/CMakeLists.txt:15 builds a camera demo that creates a gz-rendering scene (examples/save_image/main.cc:59-68), constructs an sdf::Sensor with a CameraSensor (main.cc:108-124) and calls Manager::RunOnce once (main.cc:130-131); examples/loop_sensor/CMakeLists.txt:13 builds a demo that requires an operator-supplied SDF file (main.cc:36-46) and loops over a local Manager (main.cc:120-124). Neither example is a product device interface; both take their scene, sensors and world parameters from caller code.

The metadata is a Gazebo/CMake package, not a ROS package: package.xml:13-22 depends only on gz-cmake, gz-common, gz-math, gz-msgs, gz-rendering, gz-tools, gz-transport, gz-utils and sdformat, and package.xml:26-28 declares <build_type>cmake</build_type>. There is no roscpp, rclcpp, rospy or rclpy dependency; a recursive search of the pinned tree finds no .msg, .srv, .action or .launch file and no ROS client include. package.xml:2 uses the ROS package-format 2 schema only to describe this CMake package. The runtime transport is gz-transport: src/Lidar.cc:126-131 advertises gz::msgs::LaserScan on this->Topic(), and src/Sensor.cc:247-254 advertises the sensor's set_rate service on the gz-transport node. Topic names and sensor parameters are runtime SDF input (examples/save_image/main.cc:108-113), so the clone declares no fixed ROS endpoint, message, service or action that a RosDriver could cite. src/Lidar.cc:264 confirms ROS access is external: "the ros_gz plugin is using the laserscan.proto 'frame' field".

The sensor classes also require a host simulation: include/gz/sensors/Sensor.hh:50-55 calls Sensor 'a base for all sensor classes' that parses SDF and updates at the right time; src/Manager.cc:69-77 only stores sensor objects, and src/Manager.cc:80-87 only calls Update on them with a caller-supplied time. Rendering sensors need an external gz-rendering Scene (CameraSensor::SetScene at examples/save_image/main.cc:124), and the README states the library relies on Gazebo Rendering and Gazebo Physics (README.md:20). The library itself provides no physics step, environment reset, action space or deployed sensor instance; the SDF files under test/ and examples/ are test or demo inputs, examples/loop_sensor/main.cc:36-46 requires an operator-supplied SDF path and loads it, and examples/loop_sensor/sensors.sdf is one such demo world, not a fixed device configuration. The card's entry_symbols and models are empty, and the registry records NO_ENTRY_SYMBOL for this package.

Consequently this is a component/asset library that needs a scenario and a host simulator to become a device; it is not the device itself. A RosDriver cannot be written without inventing ROS endpoints and types, and a direct Python native cannot express the C++ class under the gate's AST or be run without building and embedding the library, which rule 1 forbids. No SDK helper exists for gz-transport. If the card is instead treated as a sensor device, the correct outcome would be HELPER_MISSING for the missing gz-transport runtime, not a completed integration. No package code was written, no gate was run, task.json is unchanged, and the clone at ab16088a835409ab5d974e48beb622e30f16d9bd is unmodified (git status clean). No hardware was attached, no upstream code was imported, installed or run, and no network or pip install was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Accepted the skip proposal NOT_A_DEVICE after reading the cited lines at the pin: gz-sensors is the C++ Gazebo sensor-model library (README.md:18-20), package.xml is a CMake package over gz-* dependencies with no roscpp, rclcpp, rospy or rclpy (package.xml:13-28), the tree has no .msg, .srv, .action or .launch file and no ROS client include, its runtime transport is gz-transport (src/Lidar.cc:126-131, src/Sensor.cc:247-254), and the only executables are examples that need a caller-built scene or an operator-supplied SDF. One imprecision is noted, not edited: the notes name two of the three example executables (examples/imu_noise also builds sensor_noise), which does not change the conclusion. The author wrote no package code; the only file the review added is the check-report.json of the reviewer's gate re-run (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package), which the export ignores.
